chapter: Later career and The Benny Goodman Story
title: WNEW staff job and teaching at Juilliard
summary: Wilson recalls his radio staff job at WNEW and why Schuman wanted a jazz improvisation course.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Let's see, I think I finished with the Goodman group in 1945, and maybe after that, I got the 400 Restaurant job, and I took a job with -- a staff job with WNEW which had live musicians on staff in those days, it was the leading independent in New York, radio, in 1945, and also I went on the faculty, the summer school faculty of the Juilliard School, teaching jazz piano improvisation, because the new President, William Shuman, had come in and replaced Dean Wedge, And how I happened to be there was that William Shuman composed the overture to the second act of the Seven Lively Arts, for the symphony orchestra

in the pit conducted by Maurice Bramovitz, and I got to talking to William Shuman during rehearsals, and he thought it'd be a good idea for me to come up and join the faculty of Juliard and teach piano jazz improvisation, because many of the students had a strictly classical background, and many of them could not make a living playing classical music after they graduated, and a lot of them were not qualified to be good teachers, but maybe if they got a taste of the jazz music, they might get in to studio work or jazz playing, and still have a career in music, and not have those years of training at Juliard wasted.
